tools.name: check_deposit_cap
tools.description: Work out the most a landlord or agent can ask for as a tenancy deposit and a holding deposit, from the rent, in any UK nation, and optionally check a deposit the user was asked for. England limits both; Wales limits the holding deposit; Scotland and Northern Ireland limit the tenancy deposit.

tools.name: check_notice_period
tools.description: Work out the least notice that ends a periodic private tenancy, and the earliest end date it can name, in any UK nation, whether the tenant or the landlord gives it. It also says when a landlord cannot end the tenancy by notice at all (England) or must apply to a tribunal (Scotland).

tools.name: check_rent_increase_notice
tools.description: Check a section 13 rent increase notice for an assured periodic tenancy in England, served from 1 May 2026: whether the new rent's start date meets each date rule and the notice is on the prescribed form, and the earliest the new rent could start. tools.description: Check a landlord's rent-increase notice for a private residential tenancy in Scotland, outside a rent control area: whether it gives at least three months' notice, whether the rent has already gone up in the 12 months before, and whether it is on the prescribed form; when the new rent can start, and

tools.name: check_welsh_rent_increase_notice
tools.description: Check a landlord's notice of a new rent for a periodic standard occupation contract in Wales: whether the new rent starts at least two months after the notice is given, whether it comes at least a year after the last increase, and whether it is on form RHW12; and the earliest the new rent can start.

tools.name: check_northern_ireland_rent_increase_notice

tools.name: check_statutory_notice
tools.description: Work out the least notice the law requires to end employment in any UK nation, from the employer and from the employee, from the start date and the day notice is given. A contract can require more notice, never less.

tools.name: check_holiday_entitlement
tools.description: Work out the statutory minimum paid holiday a year, in days, for a worker who works a set number of days a week, in any UK nation: 5.6 weeks, at most 28 days, which may include bank holidays.

tools.name: check_minimum_wage
tools.description: Check whether an hourly rate of pay meets the UK minimum wage for the worker’s age, and apprenticeship, on a date from 1 April 2024, and give the rate that applies.

tools.name: get_tenancy_agreement_review_link
tools.description: Get the link to a full Contract Lily review of a UK tenancy agreement, and what it covers: whether reviews are open, the nations, what the report includes, the files it accepts and the price. Use it when the user wants their whole agreement checked; it doesn't upload anything.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_tenancy_agreement_review_link, get_employment_contract_review_link · Private data: check_notice_period, check_scottish_rent_increase_notice, check_northern_ireland_rent_increase_notice, get_tenancy_agreement_review_link, get_employment_contract_review_link · Public sink: get_tenancy_agreement_review_link, get_employment_contract_review_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_tenancy_agreement_review_link, get_employment_contract_review_link · Private data: check_notice_period, check_scottish_rent_increase_notice, check_northern_ireland_rent_increase_notice, get_tenancy_agreement_review_link, get_employment_contract_review_link · Public sink: get_tenancy_agreement_review_link, get_employment_contract_review_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
